title: Russia and Ukraine begin 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner exchange agreed in Istanbul
body:
On 23 May 2025, Russia and Ukraine began the exchange of prisoners agreed at their talks in Istanbul on 16 May. On the first day, each side returned 270 prisoners of war and 120 civilians. President Volodymyr Zelensky put the total for that day at 390 people returned to Ukraine.

The swap was part of a 1,000-for-1,000 formula. Zelensky had called the Istanbul talks "perhaps the only real result" of the first direct meeting between the sides in years. He said he expected the exchange to continue on Saturday and Sunday, 24 and 25 May. Vladimir Rogov, a Russian-appointed official, said it would run from Friday to Sunday. Russia's Defence Ministry said only that it would continue "in the coming days."

Ukraine's Defense Minister Rustem Umerov called the process "complex and sensitive." Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow had received a list of prisoners from Kyiv.

US President Donald Trump called the exchange "major" and congratulated both sides. He wrote, "This could lead to something big???" If completed, the 1,000-for-1,000 swap would be the largest such exchange in three years. The previous exchange, on 6 May, had been a one-for-one swap of 205 soldiers on each side. Reporting on 23 May did not yet describe the results of the later stages of the exchange.
